doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Depression childhood and its effect on his music
summary: His poor childhood during the Depression after his parents split may inform his feeling for ballads.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Do you feel that that has put a depth in your playing? An emotion? Because there is word that your ballad playing is just beautiful.

Well thanks that’s a nice compliment. I don’t know. I think that that, coupled with the depression, you know I’m a child of — when I started taking piano lessons the depression hit this country. “Depression” was a wonderful word for it. That was a very depressed time. You can’t put it in words. Everybody was broke. And my parents broke up, I was left with my mother, my mother had to raise me, she had to take a job in a restaurant, so © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

we were very poor. I think that had a little to do with the, if I have any feeling for music it probably helped a little to — sometimes I can use the music to remember those days. I’m not saying it’s a necessity, you know, but it probably helps a little.
